text:
The Golden Knights' three-game winning streak is over, and it ended in a 6-2 rout at T-Mobile Arena. Tampa Bay scored twice in the first five minutes of the second period's stretch of six goals in 14 minutes of game time, and it ran away from there. Anthony Cirelli scored twice in the second period, Nikita Kucherov had a goal and two assists, and Brandon Hagel, John Carlson and Victor Hedman each scored once.

The scoreboard flatters the Lightning, though. By expected goals, which measure the quality of each team's chances, Vegas led 3.93 to 2.95 and deserved to win about 65 percent of the time, meaning it took the game in roughly two of every three simulated replays of the same shots. Vegas outshot Tampa Bay 34 to 21 and owned the third period, out-chancing the Lightning 1.39 to 0.67. Its best look came from Braeden Bowman, a 38 percent chance in the third that Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped. Vasilevskiy faced 34 shots, allowed two, and saved about two goals more than the chances he faced would typically produce. Hedman's goal in the second period came on a chance of under 1 percent.

At the other end, Carter Hart allowed six goals on 21 shots, about three more than those shots deserved. Vegas had scored twice in the first period, Ivan Barbashev's snap shot and a shorthanded goal from Mark Stone that tied it at 2, but it never led. The Lightning have won three straight. The Golden Knights go back to work with that three-game run behind them.
